solution: \(\det(\operatorname{Adj} A) = (\det A)^{2}\); computing \(\det(\operatorname{Adj} A) = 4\) gives \(\det A = 2\) (positive, as required). Then \(X = A^{-1}B = \frac{1}{\det A}(\operatorname{Adj} A)B\). With \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\), \((\operatorname{Adj} A)B = \begin{bmatrix} 1-1-2 \\ 1+1-2 \\ 1+1+2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}\); dividing by \(2\) gives \(X = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\). Matches option A.
